summary: A Cibola National Forest lookout on La Mosca Peak, with construction reported in 1939; the current CL-100 cab dates to the 1960s.

facts.design: CL-100 series 14x14 ft metal cab with catwalk on a 10-ft concrete block base
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Cibola National Forest (Mount Taylor Ranger District)

events.note: Construction of a lookout structure on La Mosca Peak reported June to October 1939; a 1940 survey disk is stamped on the doorstep
Register gives 1960 for the current CL-100 cab, which it says replaced an L-4 lookout from the early 1930s
Register visit report, July 30, 2017: good condition, staffed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register's 1960 and the 2020 review's 1960s refer to the current cab. The 1939 newspaper items and the 1940 survey disk show construction on the peak in 1939-40, so 1960 is not the earliest building date. Whether the register's L-4 lookout was the same structure is not settled by these sources.

notes_for_editor: Early history unclear: 1939 newspaper items and a 1940 survey disk show construction on the peak, but the register's account of an earlier L-4 lookout is not reconciled with them. Current-status evidence is the 2017 register visit; no 2020s staffing confirmation was found. Access level not set: no visitor or road-access information read. The record's kind two_story matches the firelookout.org NM index (2-Story Cab) but was not checked against a page read here.
